Interactive Previews for snazzieR Tables

Source: R/preview.R
snazzieR_table.Rd

The LaTeX tables returned by model.summary.table, ANOVA.summary.table, eigen.summary, pls.summary, ridge.summary and format.pls carry the class "snazzieR_table". This lets them show a readable preview when a chunk is run interactively (for example with the play button in the RStudio or Positron editor), while knitting produces exactly the same LaTeX as before.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'snazzieR_table'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'snazzieR_table'
knit_print(x, options = list(), ...)

Arguments

x

A "snazzieR_table" object.

...

Further arguments passed to the underlying print method.

options

Chunk options, passed on by knitr.

Value

x, invisibly.

Details

When a document is being knitted, printing is handed straight to the underlying knitr/kableExtra method, so compiled output does not change. Outside of knitting, the preview style is controlled by the option snazzieR.preview:

"auto"

(default) An HTML preview in RStudio or Positron, a plain-text preview in other interactive sessions, and the raw LaTeX in non-interactive sessions.

"html"

Always render an HTML preview.

"text"

Always print a plain-text preview.

"latex"

Always print the raw LaTeX source.

Examples

model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)
tbl <- model.summary.table(model, title = "Fuel Economy")

# Force a plain-text preview
old <- options(snazzieR.preview = "text")
print(tbl)
#> == Fuel Economy — mpg = 37.23 - 3.878*wt - 0.03177*hp ==
#> 
#> 
#> Term          Estimate   Std.Error   P.Value   Signif.   Statistic            Value
#> ------------  ---------  ----------  --------  --------  ---------------  ---------
#> (Intercept)   37.22727   1.59879     0         :3        MSE                6.09524
#> wt            -3.87783   0.63273     0         :3        MSE adj.           6.72578
#> hp            -0.03177   0.00903     0.00145   :)        df                29.00000
#>                                                          R-squared          0.82679
#>                                                          R-squared adj.     0.81484
#> significance codes:  :3 < 0.001,  :) < 0.01,  :/ < 0.05
#> 
options(old)
